Today on the show is Aydon Stefanopoulos!

Aydon is a graduated senior out of Los Gatos High School in California. He will be a rising freshman this fall at UCLA. 

Aydon holds PRs of 1:51 for 800m, 4:06 for 1600m, 8:57 for 3200m, and 14:52 for 5K XC. He is the 2023 CIF D2 XC State Champion and a 2023 NXN qualifier.

Aydon and I had one of the most unpolished, raw, candid conversations I have ever had on The Sunday Shakeout. This was not an episode filled with positivity and glorified realities of the mental and physical side of our sport. We dive into the nitty gritty side of the sport of running. It's real, down to earth-dialogue.

As a junior, Aydon became a state champ and ran at NXN. This set a high bar to live up to his senior year. Unfortunately, however, Aydon has struggled with injuries and underperforming this past year. He failed to repeat at State XC, as well as qualify for NXN. He also did not have the redemption that he wanted this track season, despite setting PRs across multiple distances.

Aydon, in this episode, openly admits his struggles with confidence, self-doubt, and the mental toll of injuries and underperformance. Rather than just focusing on the accomplishments, he highlights the mistakes, regrets, and the emotional fallout of failure. He talks about being "not proud" of parts of his senior year, showing maturity and humility. 

Now, you might be asking:
"Why would I listen to such a melancholy podcast episode?"

Because despite setbacks, disappointments and the raw realities presented in my conversation with Aydon, he had a couple of mindset shifts: 

1. Moving from chasing perfection to valuing long-term health and enjoyment of the sport. Through setbacks and injuries, Aydon shares interesting insights on the importance of under training. Sounds crazy. But worth a listen.

2. Aydon's excitement about the next chapter at UCLA stems from a desire to learn, adapt, and improve, rather than prove anything. His ability to embrace uncertainty is instructive for all of us in the pursuit of excellence in our running careers.

I hope you enjoy this episode of The Sunday Shakeout!
